eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket favors California Governor Gavin Newsom at 25% implied probability for the 2028 Democratic presidential nomination, driven by his executive record, national fundraising prowess, and early positioning through media appearances and anti-Trump rhetoric following the 2024 election. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez trails at 8% on progressive appeal and social media dominance, while Jon Ossoff's 7% reflects his Georgia Senate wins and moderate Southern draw. Kamala Harris lags at 5% amid post-loss scrutiny. Differentiation hinges on ideological lanes—centrist electability versus left-wing energy—and metrics like 2026 midterm performances, donor networks, and Biden-era endorsements, any of which could consolidate the fragmented primary field.
